A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RCPO research. Their complete main texts and Appendices A–G are readable, and corresponding equations, figures, tables and experiments can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original preference-tuning experiments on Llama-3-8B-Instruct and Gemma-2-9B-it, including benchmark results, alternative-judge evaluations and generated-response examples.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds Mistral experiments, UltraFeedback evaluation, ablations, efficiency measurements and qualitative examples.

M1.justification: The RCPO framework, MNL and Mallows-RMJ training objectives, entropy proxy and final smoothed losses in Table 1 remain unchanged. Appendix C corrects its smoothing description to agree with those losses; it does not establish a different training procedure. Additional models and ranking lengths instantiate the existing method.

E1.justification: v2 extends evaluation to an in-distribution UltraFeedback test scenario, alongside the retained AlpacaEval 2 and Arena-Hard evaluations. UltraFeedback was already used for training, so this does not introduce a new domain. Appendix G also replaces equation solving with factual explanation and text simplification. Mistral adds a model configuration rather than a task.

E2.justification: v2 Tables 2 and 10 add DPO-AllPairs, which Table 2 defines as DPO trained on pairwise comparisons implied by top-2 rankings. Existing comparators remain, including those in the unchanged GPT-5-mini comparison. This is a focused addition to the baseline set.

E3.justification: New protocols include evaluating 1,961 UltraFeedback test prompts against their chosen responses using GPT-4.1-mini and training Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2. Section 4.3 and Appendix F.3 introduce ranking-length, assortment-size, training-progress and beta sweeps, together with timing comparisons. These substantially expand the experimental design without establishing revisions to the retained Llama/Gemma benchmark settings.

E4.justification: v1 has cross-judge checks and qualitative examples but no corresponding systematic ablation suite. v2 adds tests of ranking length, assortment size, beta sensitivity, sample efficiency, and pairwise decomposition versus direct ranked training, including computational costs. Appendix G removes the equation-solving case and adds two different cases. The earlier cross-judge analysis is retained, not newly introduced.

E5.justification: Both versions report AlpacaEval standard errors and Arena-Hard 95% confidence intervals. v2 extends the standard-error convention to its new UltraFeedback results but introduces no new statistical estimation procedure, significance test, seed information or repeated-run count.

E6.justification: Shared Llama/Gemma benchmark scores and GPT-5-mini results are unchanged. Substantial new results include UltraFeedback WR of 68.91% for Mallows-RMJ-PO-Top-2 versus 62.36% for DPO, Mistral outcomes, DPO-AllPairs results, and ablation/efficiency measurements. The new Mistral Arena-Hard results favor SimPO, 19.3% versus 16.9% for Mallows-RMJ-PO-Top-2. Qualitative outputs also change in Appendix G.

T1.justification: Appendix C changes the smoothing approximation from sigma(-beta*x) to sigma(-x), resolving an extra scaling factor relative to the retained Table 1 objectives. The assumptions and Theorems 1–5 remain unchanged. Rewriting the MNL denominators and proofs into equivalent likelihood expressions does not constitute additional theoretical results.

C1.justification: The introduction narrows the benefit from avoiding information loss inherent in pairwise conversion to mitigating information inefficiency. The abstract explicitly extends its empirical assertion to three model families and both in-distribution and out-of-distribution settings. The central MLE-unification claim, two representative choice models and conclusion remain.

C2.justification: v1 conjectures that noise may limit gains beyond top-2. v2 substantially expands interpretation through annotation-difficulty, negative-response, batch-capacity, sample-efficiency and pairwise-expansion explanations in Section 4.3 and Appendix F.3. New qualitative examples are explicitly described as illustrative rather than fact-checked. Conversely, the revised cross-model superiority statement drops v1's qualification about LC and overlooks SimPO's Mistral Arena-Hard lead.

D1.justification: v2 newly identifies the modified TRL DPO Trainer and DPO Config, states that code and training scripts accompany supplementary materials, specifies the evaluation-generation GPU, supplies the Mistral model identifier and reports training times. These are additional disclosures; the supplied PDFs do not allow verification of the supplementary code.

R1.justification: v2 adds related-work citations for K-order ranking, permutative alignment and multi-level preferences, plus reward-model and evaluation references. It removes Luce and Plackett citations from the MNL discussion and drops the claim that ranked choice was first formally studied by Feng and Tang. Overall positioning remains similar; the additional published LiPO entry represents an already cited work.

P1.justification: v2 edits the abstract, terminology and explanatory prose, adds the conference header, and introduces experimental subsections. The main conceptual narrative, section sequence and Appendix A–G organization remain recognizable. Most expansion supplies new scientific content rather than extensive rewriting or restructuring.

P2.justification: Tables 2–3 expand structurally to display UltraFeedback, DPO-AllPairs and Mistral results. v2 adds ablation/timing Tables 4, 8 and 10 and learning/sensitivity Figures 3–4, redraws Figure 2a, and replaces one qualitative table with two new examples. This substantially expands the evidence displays; the retained cross-judge table is merely relocated and renumbered.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially addresses v1's lack of empirical justification for feedback-size choices and direct ranked training versus pairwise expansion: Section 4.3 and Appendix F.3 add relevant ablations and cost comparisons. Additional evaluation settings strengthen validation, and removing v1's incorrectly labeled equation-solving success improves qualitative reliability. These gains outweigh limited reporting problems: the new cross-model superiority wording overlooks SimPO's Mistral advantage, and the claimed 9.47-point UltraFeedback gain over IPO conflicts with the 10.47-point difference in Table 2.
